newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 22.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page on January 22:

WASHINGTON - The House voted overwhelmingly to reprimand House Speaker Newt Gingrich and order him to pay an unprecedented $300,000 penalty, the first time in the House's history it has disciplined a speaker for ethical wrongdoing.
WASHINGTON - A self-proclaimed revolutionary, Newt Gingrich has always skated on the edge of political respectability, even as he concedes that he finds it difficult to discern where that edge is.

WASHINGTON - Democratic National Committee officials announced that the party no longer will accept contributions from foreign nationals or the American subsidiaries of foreign corporations and will put a $100,000 cap on all future "soft money" donations.
SANTA MONICA, Calif. - A plaintiff's attorney described O. J. Simpson as a savage, remorseless murderer and chronic liar who left a trail of overwhelming, irrefutable physical evidence of his guilt.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton announced that in an effort to "reach out to Republicans" he is proposing new funding cuts in Medicare, one of the principal obstacles to a balanced budget agreement last year.
WASHINGTON - Parents who suspect their children are using drugs soon will be able to use a government-approved home drug testing kit.

WASHINGTON - The evening turned sour about 12.45 a.m., right after President Clinton waved goodbye to the inaugural ball crowd at the Omni Shoreham Hotel and thousands of guests converged en masse to collect their coats, a chore which took some more than two hours.
